title: Eighteenmile reported point-source discharge: history and wastewater volume
sections: Reported point-source discharge: original scope

The selected original EPA records cover four permitted facilities. This study retains permit, reporting feature, monitoring location and pollutant parameter as separate identities. Source capture: 2026-10-13T01:22:10Z.
Historical coverage comprises 20 original series, 321 series-year records and 3046 selected original monitoring periods. 199 historical series-years have twelve unique numeric monthly periods.

Reported effluent amounts describe the selected discharge sources. The current relation to USGS-02186702 is retained as geographic context. Published annual outputs, complete monthly-period sums, same-month comparisons and the separate existing 2023 calendar-weighted scientific calculation keep their original bases.
Five-year phosphorus context

The current upstream phosphorus cohort is 955.70 kg in 2025, compared with 520.70 kg in 2024. The 83.54% change compares with the lowest year in this five-year window; 2025 remains close to 2023 and within the original 2021–2025 range of 520.70–985.58 kg.
Each total combines the same three currently upstream permit series while preserving their original EPA features. Suspended-solids and phosphorus masses are separate parameter-specific totals.
Exact current-year phosphorus comparisons

Upper, Middle and Milliken share January–August. Their phosphorus load changes from 655.73 to 948.33 kg (292.60 kg, 44.62%). Milliken changes 332.35 kg, Upper -23.59 kg and Middle -16.16 kg. Pendleton–Clemson remains the separate downstream January–July comparison.
Reported volume and load intensity

rows: Load per volume, kg / million US gallons

sections: For each matched month M = V × I, with M in kg, V in million US gallons and I = M/V. The symmetric volume component is (V1−V0)×(I0+I1)/2; the intensity component is (I1−I0)×(V0+V1)/2. These two components sum to the original load change.

rows: Current upstream Total phosphorus as P

sections: These are descriptive components of the original mass/volume identity. Original EPA average-concentration values and measurement choices remain separate fields. Operational causes require separate process evidence. Monthly components are summed; a separately retained whole-window calculation has a different allocation.
Original monthly phosphorus measurements

Every selected Milliken monthly row uses the original Average Quantity measurement choice. June and July have the largest 2026 loads in this exact comparison window. The retained paired-month table includes source response IDs, exact JSON pointers, original quantity/concentration fields, qualifiers, NODI and QC flags.
Coverage and original source choices

30 original series/windows and 295 exact matched months have complete positive published-volume support. Four parameter-specific upstream cohorts are retained. Two quarterly/ineligible windows remain explicit in the coverage table.

Full-year comparisons require twelve unique numeric monthly periods in both years. Current-year comparisons use the exact intersection of numeric original months. Middle Eighteenmile current total nitrogen retains months 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8. Its unsupported April remains outside that comparison.

The original queries retain p_est=N and ND=ZERO. Published annual p_est=N and p_est=Y results remain separate from monthly sums; a p_est=N query alone does not establish an unscaled annual sum. Total nitrogen, ammonia and nitrate remain separate species. Future placeholders and nonnumeric periods remain original context.

EPA defines PollutantLoad0 as kg per reporting period and WastewaterFlow as million gallons per reporting period. Original AvgConcentration0 is retained in mg/L. Calculations use the original displayed numeric values; detailed output rounds only after full-precision arithmetic.
